W1 Foresight Advent Prudence
Advent 1 — "Stay awake, be ready"
▸
Advent opens with the command to watch. Foresight is the virtue of looking ahead, reading the signs, and anticipating what God is bringing.

PRO.27.12		 The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty. This we had before, Pro 22:3. Note, 1. Evil may be foreseen. The prudent see danger ahead and take refuge, defining foresight as wise anticipation of what is coming.

I. God declares the end from the beginning; all true foresight is rooted in His sovereign omniscience.

Joseph's God-given interpretation of Pharaoh's dreams exemplifies foresight that saves nations from famine.

The psalmist acknowledges God desires truth in the inward being, praying for deep interior honesty.
W10 Integrity Ordinary Time I Justice
OT Week 5 — "You are salt and light"
▸
Salt that loses its flavor is thrown out. Light hidden under a basket serves no one. Integrity means being the same person inside and out — radiant and uncompromised.
Day Theme Reference BSB Text Commentary Reflection Rationale
Sunday Define Psalms 25:21
PSA.25.21		 May integrity and uprightness preserve me, because I wait for You. David, encouraged by the promises he had been meditating upon, here renews his addresses to God, and concludes the psalm, as he began, with professions of dependence upon God and desire towards him. I. He lays open before God the calamitous condition he was in. David declares integrity and uprightness as the character that guards the one who waits on the Lord.
Monday Root Deuteronomy 32:4
DEU.32.4		 He is the Rock, His work is perfect; all His ways are just. A God of faithfulness without injustice, righteous and upright is He. Here is, I. A commanding preface or introduction to this song of Moses, Deu 32:1, Deu 32:2. He begins, 1. God is the Rock whose works are perfect; all His ways are just, establishing integrity's divine origin.
Tuesday Model Job 2:3
JOB.2.3		 Then the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered My servant Job? For there is no one on earth like Him, a man who is blameless and upright, Who fears God and shuns evil. God Himself testifies that Job held fast to his integrity despite devastating, undeserved suffering.
Wednesday Practice Matthew 5:13

I. Ye are the salt of the earth. Jesus commands believers to be salt that retains its savor—integrity lived visibly in daily practice.
Thursday Obstacle Proverbs 11:3
PRO.11.3		 The integrity of the upright guides them, but the perversity of the faithless destroys them. The crookedness of the treacherous destroys them, revealing duplicity as integrity's chief and deadly enemy.

MAT.5.14		 You are the light of the world. A city on a hill cannot be hidden. I. Ye are the salt of the earth. Those who walk in integrity become a city on a hill, their light an undeniable witness to all.
Saturday Prayer Psalms 26:1
PSA.26.1		 Vindicate me, O LORD! For I have walked with integrity; I have trusted in the LORD without wavering. David prays for God to vindicate him, declaring he has walked in integrity and trusted without wavering.
W11 Reasoning Ordinary Time I Prudence
OT Week 6 — "You have heard it said… but I say to you"
▸
Jesus deepens the Mosaic Law through rigorous moral reasoning. He does not abolish but fulfills — showing that reason illuminated by faith goes deeper than the letter.
Day Theme Reference BSB Text Commentary Reflection Rationale
Sunday Define Isaiah 1:18
ISA.1.18		 “Come now, let us reason together,” says the LORD. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow; though they are as red as crimson, they will become like wool. Though God had rejected their services as insufficient to atone for their sins while they persisted in them, yet he does not reject them as in a hopeless condition, but here calls upon them to forsake their sins, which hindered the acceptance of their services, and then all would be well. God invites His people to reason together with Him, defining reasoning as a divine-human dialogue toward truth.
Monday Root Proverbs 2:6
PRO.2.6		 For the LORD gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding. Job had asked, long before this, Where shall wisdom be found? Whence cometh wisdom? (Job 28:12, Job 28:20) and he had given this general answer (v. The Lord Himself is the source of knowledge and understanding, grounding all sound reasoning in God.

The Bereans modeled virtuous reasoning by examining the Scriptures daily to test Paul's teaching.

Christ having laid down these principles, that Moses and the prophets were still to be their rulers, but that the scribes and Pharisees were to be no longer their rulers, proceeds to expound the law in some particular instances, and to vindicate it from the corrupt glosses which those expositors had put upon it. Jesus deepens the law—'but I say to you'—training disciples to reason beyond the letter to the heart.

Love abounding in knowledge and discernment is the blessed fruit of Spirit-guided reasoning.

PSA.139.23		 Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my concerns. Here the psalmist makes application of the doctrine of God's omniscience, divers ways. I. He acknowledges, with wonder and thankfulness, the care God had taken of him all his days, Psa 139:17, Psa 139:18. The psalmist prayerfully invites God to search and know his anxious thoughts, surrendering reasoning to God.
W12 Forgiveness Ordinary Time I Temperance
OT Week 7 — "Love your enemies"
▸
The most radical command in the Gospel. Forgiveness is the temperance virtue that restrains our instinct for retaliation and frees us to love beyond merit.

W13 Practical Wisdom Ordinary Time I Prudence
OT Week 8 — "The wise man built on rock"
▸
The capstone of the Sermon on the Mount. Prudence — practical wisdom — is the master virtue that builds one's life on the solid foundation of Christ's teaching.

W14 Restraint Lent Temperance
Lent 1 — Ash Wednesday / Temptation in the Desert
▸
Lent begins with fasting. Jesus refuses bread, spectacle, and power. Restraint — the habit of saying no to legitimate goods for a higher purpose — is the gateway to Lenten conversion.

A city with broken walls pictures the soul without restraint—naming the virtue by its absence.

2TI.1.7		 For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control. Here is an exhortation and excitation of Timothy to his duty (Ti2 1:6): I put thee in remembrance. Jesus answers Satan's first desert temptation with Scripture, modeling perfect restraint over bodily appetite.

▸

Sunday Define Isaiah 58:6

The apostle, having thus excited and enforced sacred love from the great pattern and motive of it, the love that is and dwells in God himself, proceeds to recommend it further by other considerations; and he recommends it in both the branches of it, both as love to God, and love to our brother or Christian neighbour. I. All genuine friendliness flows from God's prior love: 'We love because He first loved us.'
Tuesday Model 1 Samuel 18:1
1SA.18.1		 After David had finished speaking with Saul, the souls of Jonathan and David were knit together, and Jonathan loved him as himself. That Saul, who was now in possession of the crown, reposed a confidence in him, God so ordering it, that he might by his preferment at court be prepared for future service. Wednesday Practice John 15:12
JHN.15.12		 This is My commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you. Christ, who is love itself, is here discoursing concerning love, a fourfold love. I. Concerning the Father's love to him; and concerning this he here tells us, 1. Jesus commands the practice: 'Love one another as I have loved you'—the New Commandment enacted daily.

A contemplative blessing: 'How good and pleasant it is when brothers dwell together in unity.'
W26 Diligence Easter Temperance
Ascension / Easter 7 — "Go and make disciples of all nations"
▸
The Great Commission demands industrious effort. Diligence — the measured, sustained application of energy to the work at hand — is how the Church carries out the Ascension mandate.
Day Theme Reference BSB Text Commentary Reflection Rationale
Sunday Define Proverbs 12:24
PRO.12.24		 The hand of the diligent will rule, but laziness ends in forced labor. Industry is the way to preferment. The hand of the diligent will rule, directly defining diligence as the path to fruitful authority.

The spiteful scornful reflection which Sanballat and Tobiah cast upon the Jews for their attempt to build the wall about Jerusalem. Nehemiah's people rebuilt the wall with wholehearted diligence, modeling persistent labor for God's purposes.
Wednesday Practice Matthew 28:19-20
MAT.28.19-20		 Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey all that I have commanded you. [jamieson-fausset-brown] Jesus commands us to go and make disciples of all nations — diligent mission echoing the Ascension mandate.
Thursday Obstacle Proverbs 6:9

Slothfulness is as sure a way to poverty, though not so short a way, as rash suretiship. The sluggard's love of sleep is the vice diligence must overcome: 'How long will you lie there?'

I. Diligence to the end secures the full assurance of hope — perseverance yields confident eternal reward.

A closing prayer asking God to establish the work of our hands, consecrating diligent labor to Him.
W27 Creativity Easter Prudence
Pentecost — The Holy Spirit descends in fire and wind
▸
The Spirit speaks in every tongue, invents new ways to reach every heart. Creativity — the prudence virtue of finding unexpected solutions — is the Spirit's signature gift.
Day Theme Reference BSB Text Commentary Reflection Rationale

EXO.35.31-32		 And He has filled Him with the Spirit of God, with skill, ability, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship, to design artistic works in gold, silver, and bronze, Here is the divine appointment of the master-workmen, that there might be no strife for the office, and that all who were employed in the work might take direction from, and give account to, these general inspectors; for God is the God of order and not of confusion. Observe, 1. God fills Bezalel with the Spirit, granting skill, intelligence, and creativity for sacred work.

GEN.1.1		 In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. In these verses we have the work of creation in its epitome and in its embryo. I. In its epitome, Gen 1:1, where we find, to our comfort, the first article of our creed, that God the Father Almighty is the Maker of heaven and earth, and as such we believe in him. God as Creator is the ultimate source and origin of all creative power and imagination.

EXO.31.3-4		 And I have filled Him with the Spirit of God, with skill, ability, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship, to design artistic works in gold, silver, and bronze, A great deal of fine work God had ordered to be done about the tabernacle; the materials the people were to provide, but who must put them into form? Moses himself was learned in all the learning of the Egyptians, nay, he was well acquainted with the words of God, and the visions of the Almighty; but he knew not how to engrave or embroider. Bezalel models Spirit-filled creativity, devising artistic designs in gold, stone, and wood for God's glory.

COL.3.23-24		 Whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, as for the Lord and not for men, because you know that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord as your reward. The epistles which are most taken up in displaying the glory of divine grace, and magnifying the Lord Jesus, are the most particular and distinct in pressing the duties of the several relations. Work wholeheartedly as for the Lord, channeling creative energy into every endeavor with purposeful devotion.
Thursday Obstacle Matthew 25:25
MAT.25.25		 So I was afraid and went out and hid your talent in the ground. See, you have what belongs to you.’ And I was afraid,.... The Persic version adds, "to negotiate with thy money": he was afraid, lest by trading he should not gain what his Lord expected; and most of all, lest he should lose the talent itself; and dreaded his Lord's austerity, should that be the case, fearing that he would have no mercy on him. [john-gill] The fearful servant buried his talent; fear and sloth are the enemies of creative faithfulness.

ACT.2.4		 And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them. When, and where, this was done, which are particularly noted, for the greater certainty of the thing. At Pentecost the Spirit unleashes new tongues and bold expression — creativity's ultimate transformative fruit.

PSA.51.10		 Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. I. See here what David prays for. A plea for God to create a clean heart renews the spirit and opens space for fresh inspiration.
W28 Memory Ordinary Time II Prudence
Trinity Sunday
▸
The Church recalls the deepest mystery of God's inner life. Memory — the prudence virtue of holding truth present in the mind — is how we treasure what has been revealed.
Day Theme Reference BSB Text Commentary Reflection Rationale
Sunday Define Deuteronomy 8:2

Israel is commanded to remember the whole journey God led them, defining holy memory as spiritual discipline.

PSA.143.5		 I remember the days of old; I meditate on all Your works; I consider the work of Your hands. Here, I. W29 Generous Giving Ordinary Time II Justice
Corpus Christi — "This is my Body, given for you"
▸
God holds nothing back. In the Eucharist, He gives His entire self. Generous giving — the habit of offering our substance, not just our surplus — mirrors this total gift.
Day Theme Reference BSB Text Commentary Reflection Rationale
Sunday Define 2 Corinthians 9:7
2CO.9.7		 Each one should give what He has decided in His heart to give, not out of regret or compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver. Here we have, I. Now, as to the manner in which the apostle would have the Corinthians give, observe, 1. God loves a cheerful giver — the definitive description of generous, wholehearted giving.

W30 Worship Ordinary Time II Justice
Sacred Heart of Jesus (mid-June)
▸
The Solemnity of the Sacred Heart invites us into the burning love of Christ's own heart. Worship — the virtue of rendering God the honor due to Him — is our entry into that fire.

W31 Justice Ordinary Time II Justice
Sts. Peter and Paul (June 29)
▸
Peter the rock. Paul the apostle to the nations. Together they establish the Church's order in truth and right relationship. Justice itself — giving each person what is due — is their shared legacy.
Day Theme Reference BSB Text Commentary Reflection Rationale
Sunday Define Micah 6:8
MIC.6.8		 He has shown you, O man, what is good. And what does the LORD require of you but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God? Upon the trial, judgment is given against Israel; they are convicted of injustice and ingratitude towards God, the crimes with which they stood charged. Defines justice as what God requires: act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with Him.

PSA.89.14		 Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne; loving devotion and faithfulness go before You. W32 Sound Judgment Ordinary Time II Prudence
St. Thomas the Apostle (July 3)
▸
Thomas demanded evidence. Jesus honored the demand. Sound judgment — the capacity to assess a situation rightly — leads Thomas from skepticism to the greatest confession of faith.

St. Benedict (July 11)
▸

W34 Respect Ordinary Time II Justice
St. Mary Magdalene (July 22)
▸
"Rabboni!" — Mary Magdalene greets the risen Lord with reverent awe. Respect (observance) is the justice virtue of honoring those who are set above us, beginning with Christ Himself.
Day Theme Reference BSB Text Commentary Reflection Rationale

1PE.2.17		 Treat everyone with high regard: Love the brotherhood of believers, fear God, honor the king. Tuesday Model Luke 7:44
LUK.7.44		 And turning toward the woman, He said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? Paul instructs believers to humbly regard others as more important than themselves in daily life.

Sts. Joachim and Anne (July 26)

W36 Good Counsel Ordinary Time II Prudence

▸
The kingdom parables (treasure in a field, pearl of great price) invite deliberation: what is worth everything? Good counsel is the virtue of seeking and giving wise advice before acting.
Day Theme Reference BSB Text Commentary Reflection Rationale
Sunday Define Proverbs 12:15

Our Lady of Sorrows (September 15)

Mary stands at the foot of the Cross with clear-eyed grief — no hysteria, no denial. Sobriety is the temperance of a mind that remains unclouded even in the deepest pain.

From the nature and design of the gospel. Grace teaches us to live soberly and righteously, producing godly fruit in the present age.

W43 Strategic Wisdom Ordinary Time II Prudence
Sts. Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael (September 29)
▸
Michael battles the dragon. Gabriel delivers the message. Raphael guides the journey. Strategic wisdom — the capacity to coordinate complex efforts toward victory — is the archangels' gift.

Sunday Define Proverbs 8:14
PRO.8.14		 Counsel and sound judgment are mine; I have insight and strength. God commands His angels to guard you in all your ways—a restful prayer trusting heaven's strategic care.
W44 Orderliness Ordinary Time II Temperance
St. Thérèse of Lisieux (October 1)
▸
The "Little Way" — doing small things with great love, in order. St. Thérèse found holiness not in grand gestures but in the careful ordering of daily life toward God.

W45 Playing Well Ordinary Time II Temperance
St. Francis of Assisi (Oct 4) / Our Lady of the Rosary (Oct 7)
▸
Francis preached to birds, danced with Brother Sun, and called death "Sister." Playing well — the virtue of wholesome recreation and joy — is the Franciscan charism: finding delight in God's creation.
Day Theme Reference BSB Text Commentary Reflection Rationale
Sunday Define Ecclesiastes 3:1-4

That we live in a world of changes, that the several events of time, and conditions of human life, are vastly different from one another, and yet occur promiscuously, and we are continually passing and repassing between them, as in the revolutions of every day and every year. The "hidden apostles" gave their lives for the Gospel and received the crown. Fair exchange — the justice of equal giving and receiving — is fulfilled in martyrdom: life given, eternal life received.

Sunday Define 1 Thessalonians 4:3
1TH.4.3		 For it is God’s will that you should be holy: You must abstain from sexual immorality; Here we have, I. An exhortation to abound in holiness, to abound more and more in that which is good, Th1 4:1, Th1 4:2. We may observe, 1. Paul defines God's will as sanctification, specifically that believers abstain from sexual immorality—naming chasteness directly.
Monday Root 1 Corinthians 6:19
1CO.6.19		 Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, Whom you have received from God? You are not your own; The twelfth verse and former part of the thirteenth seem to relate to that early dispute among Christians about the distinction of meats, and yet to be prefatory to the caution that follows against fornication. God is the source of chasteness because our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit who dwells within us.
Tuesday Model Matthew 25:4
MAT.25.4		 But the wise ones took oil in flasks along with their lamps. But the wise took oil,.... [john-gill] The wise virgins prepared oil for their lamps, modeling vigilant purity and readiness that echoes this week's liturgical Gospel.
Wednesday Practice 2 Timothy 2:22
2TI.2.22		 Flee from youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, together with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart. I. Paul here exhorts Timothy to beware of youthful lusts, Ti2 2:22. Though he was a holy good man, very much mortified to the world, yet Paul thought it necessary to caution him against youthful lusts: "Flee them, take all possible care and pains to keep thyself pure from them. Paul instructs Timothy to flee youthful passions and pursue righteousness, giving a concrete practice for cultivating chasteness.
Thursday Obstacle 1 Peter 2:11
1PE.2.11		 Beloved, I urge you, as foreigners and exiles, to abstain from the desires of the flesh, which war against your soul. The general rule of a Christian conversation is this, it must be honest, which it cannot be if there be not a conscientious discharge of all relative duties. The apostle here particularly treats of these distinctly. I. Peter warns that fleshly desires wage war against the soul, identifying lust as the chief obstacle to chasteness.
Friday Fruit Matthew 5:8
MAT.5.8		 Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God. Christ begins his sermon with blessings, for he came into the world to bless us (Act 3:26), as the great High Priest of our profession; as the blessed Melchizedec; as He in whom all the families of the earth should be blessed, Gen 12:3. The pure in heart are blessed because they shall see God—chasteness yields the ultimate fruit of divine intimacy.
Saturday Prayer Psalms 51:10
PSA.51.10		 Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. I. See here what David prays for. Many excellent petitions he here puts up, to which if we do but add, "for Christ's sake," they are as evangelical as any other. David's prayer for a clean heart and renewed spirit is the perfect closing petition for the grace of chasteness.
W51 Just Correction Ordinary Time II Justice
OT Week 33 — Parable of the talents / End-time accountability
▸
The master returns and settles accounts. Just correction — the virtue of righting wrongs and holding others accountable with fairness — is the theme of these eschatological parables.
Day Theme Reference BSB Text Commentary Reflection Rationale
Sunday Define Proverbs 27:5
PRO.27.5		 Better an open rebuke than love that is concealed. It is good for us to be reproved, and told of our faults, by our friends. Open rebuke is better than hidden love, defining just correction as honest, loving confrontation.
Monday Root Hebrews 12:6
HEB.12.6		 For the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and He chastises every son He receives.” Here the apostle presses the exhortation to patience and perseverance by an argument taken from the gentle measure and gracious nature of those sufferings which the believing Hebrews endured in their Christian course. I. The Lord disciplines those He loves, grounding just correction in God's fatherly authority and care.
Tuesday Model 2 Samuel 12:7
2SA.12.7		 Then Nathan said to David, “You are that man! This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you from the hand of Saul. It seems to have been a great while after David had been guilty of adultery with Bath-sheba before he was brought to repentance for it. For, when Nathan was sent to him, the child was born (Sa2 12:14), so that it was about nine months that David lay under the guilt of that sin, and, for aught that appears, unrepented of. Nathan confronts David with 'You are the man,' modeling courageous, prophetic correction of a powerful leader.
Wednesday Practice Galatians 6:1
GAL.6.1		 Brothers, if someone is caught in a trespass, you who are spiritual should restore him with a spirit of gentleness. But watch yourself, or you also may be tempted. The apostle having, in the foregoing chapter, exhorted Christians by love to serve one another (Gal 6:13), and also cautioned us (Gal 6:16) against a temper which, if indulged, would hinder us from showing the mutual love and serviceableness which he had recommended, in the beginning of this chapter he proceeds to give some further directions, which, if duly observed, would both promote the one and prevent the other of these, and render our behaviour both more agreeable to our Christian profession and more useful and comfortable to one another: particularly, I. Paul instructs the spiritual to restore the fallen gently, giving practical guidance for administering just correction.
Thursday Obstacle Matthew 25:26
MAT.25.26		 ‘You wicked, lazy servant!’ replied his master. ‘You knew that I reap where I have not sown and gather where I have not scattered seed. His Lord answered and said unto him,.... [john-gill] The master rebukes the wicked, lazy servant; neglecting accountability is the vice just correction overcomes.
Friday Fruit Proverbs 12:1
PRO.12.1		 Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but he who hates correction is stupid. We are really as we are with God. Those are happy, truly happy, for ever happy, that obtain favour of the Lord, though the world frown upon them, and they find little favour with men; for in God's favour is life, and that is the fountain of all good. Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge; receiving just correction yields wisdom and fruitful growth.
Saturday Prayer Psalms 141:5
PSA.141.5		 Let the righteous man strike me; let his rebuke be an act of loving devotion. It is oil for my head; let me not refuse it. For my prayer is ever against the deeds of the wicked. Here, I. David desires to be told of his faults. Let the righteous strike me—a prayerful openness to correction as kindness and healing oil.
W52 Fair Distribution Ordinary Time II Justice
Christ the King — "Whatever you did for the least of these…"
▸
The final Sunday of the liturgical year. Christ the King judges the nations: did you feed the hungry, clothe the naked, visit the prisoner? Fair distribution — giving to each according to their need — is the measure of His kingdom.
Day Theme Reference BSB Text Commentary Reflection Rationale
Sunday Define Matthew 25:40
MAT.25.40		 And the King will reply, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers of Mine, you did for Me.’ Then shall he also say unto them on his left hand,.... The goats, the foolish virgins, and slothful and wicked servants, depart from me: a like expression is used by him to preachers of the word, and professors of religion, that are mere nominal ones. [john-gill] Christ the King identifies fair treatment of the least as service rendered directly to Him.
Monday Root Psalms 146:7-8
PSA.146.7-8		 He executes justice for the oppressed and gives food to the hungry. The LORD sets the prisoners free, the LORD opens the eyes of the blind, the LORD lifts those who are weighed down, the LORD loves the righteous. The psalmist, having cautioned us not to trust in princes (because, if we do, we shall be miserably disappointed), here encourages us to put our confidence in God, because, if we do so, we shall be happily secured: Happy is he that has the God of Jacob for his help, that has an interest in his attributes and promises, and has them engaged for him, and whose hope is in the Lord his God. God Himself upholds the oppressed and gives food to the hungry, grounding all just distribution.
Tuesday Model Acts 4:34-35
ACT.4.34-35		 There were no needy ones among them, because those who owned lands or houses would sell their property, bring the proceeds from the sales, and lay them at the apostles’ feet for distribution to anyone as he had need. We have a general idea given us in these verses, and it is a very beautiful one, of the spirit and state of this truly primitive church; it is conspectus saeculi - a view of that age of infancy and innocence. I. The disciples loved one another dearly. The early Church distributed to each as anyone had need, modeling equitable sharing.
Wednesday Practice Isaiah 58:7
ISA.58.7		 Isn’t it to share your bread with the hungry, to bring the poor and homeless into your home, to clothe the naked when you see him, and not to turn away from your own flesh and blood? Here we have, I. The displeasure which these hypocrites conceived against God for not accepting the services which they themselves had a mighty opinion of (Isa 58:3): Wherefore have we fasted, say they, and thou seest not? Thus they went in the way of Cain, who was angry at God, and resented it as a gross affront that his offering was not accepted. God commands sharing bread with the hungry, sheltering the poor, and clothing the naked.
Thursday Obstacle Amos 5:11
AMO.5.11		 Therefore, because you trample on the poor and exact from him a tax of grain, you will never live in the stone houses you have built; you will never drink the wine from the lush vineyards you have planted. Here is, I. A very terrible threatening of destruction approaching, Amo 5:16, Amo 5:17. Since they would not take the right course to obtain the favour of God, God would take an effectual course to make them feel the weight of his displeasure. Amos condemns those who trample the poor and exact grain taxes, hoarding unjust gain.
Friday Fruit Proverbs 22:9
PRO.22.9		 A generous man will be blessed, for he shares his bread with the poor. Here is, 1. The generous person is blessed because they share their food with the poor.
Saturday Prayer Psalms 72:12
PSA.72.12		 For he will deliver the needy who cry out and the afflicted who have no helper. For he shall deliver the needy when he crieth,.... [john-gill] A royal psalm praying that the King delivers the needy and those with no helper.
